source_text:
Putatis autem nos occultare quod colimus, si delubra et aras non habemus? quod enim simulacrum Deo fingam, cum, si recte existimes, sit Dei homo ipse simulacrum? templum quod ei extruam, \'cum totus hic mundus eius opere fabricatus eum capere non possit? et cum homo latius maneam, intra unam aediculam uim tantae maiestatis includam ?
nonne Melius in nostra dedicandus est mente? in nostro immo consecrandus est pectore? hostias et uictimas Deo offeram, quas in usum mei protulit, ut reiciam ei suum munus? ingratum est, cum sit litabilis hostia bonus animus et pura mens et sincera conscientia.
igitur qui innocentiam colit, Deo supplicat, qui iustitiam, Deo libat, qui fraudibus abstinet, propitiat Deum, qui hominem periculo subripit, opimam uictimam caedit. haec nostra sacrificia, haec Dei sacra sunt: sic apud nos religiosior est ille qui iustior.
at enim quem colimus Deum, nec ostendimus nec uidemus. immo ex hoc Deum credimus, quod eum sentire possumus, uidere non possumus. in operibus enim eius et in mundi omnibus motibus uirtutem eius semper praesentem aspicimus, cum tonat, fulgurat, fulminat, cum serenat.
nec mireris, si Deum non uides: uento et flatibus omnia impelluntur, uibrantur, agitantur, et sub oculis tamen non uenit uentus et flatus. in solem adeo, qui uidendi omnibus causa est, uidere non possumus, radiis acies submouetur, obtutus intuentis hebetatur, et si diutius inspicias, omnis uisus extinguitur.
quid? ipsum solis artificem, illum luminis fontem, possis sustinere, cum te ab eius fulgoribus auertas, a fulminibus abscondas? Deum oculis carnalibus uis uidere, cum ipsam animam tuam, qua uiuificaris et loqueris, nec aspicerepossis nec tenere? sed enim Deus
actum hominis ignorat et in caelo constitutus non potest aut omnes obire aut singulos nosse. erras o homo, et falleris: unde enim Deus longe est, cum omnia caelestia terrenaque et quae extra istam orbis prouinciam sunt, Deo plena sint? ubique non tantum nobis proximus, sed infusus est.
in solem adeo rursus intende: caelo adfixus, sed terris omnibus sparsus est: pariter praesens ubique interest et miscetur omnibus, nusquam eius claritudo uiolatur.
quanto magis Deus auctor omniumac speculator omnium, a quo nullum potest esse secretum, tenebris interest, interest cogitationibus nostris, quasi alteris tenebris! non tantum sub illo agimus, sed et cum illo, ut prope dixerim, uiuimus.
thought_title: God cannot be housed or seen, yet is present everywhere
orientation: Octavius is answering Caecilius's charge that Christians have no temples, altars, or visible god, by arguing that the true God is worshiped in the mind and is known through his works and presence everywhere.
pass_a_gloss: But do you think that we hide what we worship, if we do not have shrines and altars? For what idol should I fashion for God, when, if you judge rightly, man himself is the idol of God? What temple should I build for him, when this whole world, made by his work, cannot contain him? And when I, a man, dwell rather broadly, shall I shut in the power of so great a majesty within one little shrine? Is it not better that he be dedicated in our mind? No rather, is he not to be consecrated in our heart? Shall I offer to God victims and sacrifices, which he has brought forth for my use, so that I may throw back to him his own gift? That is ungrateful, since a pleasing victim is a good spirit and a pure mind and a sincere conscience. Therefore he who cultivates innocence, prays to God; he who cultivates justice, offers to God; he who abstains from frauds, appeases God; he who snatches a man from danger, slaughters a rich victim. These are our sacrifices, these are the sacred rites of God: thus among us the more just man is the more religious. But indeed the God whom we worship, we neither show nor see. No rather, from this very fact we believe God, because we can perceive him, we cannot see him. For in his works and in all the movements of the world we behold his power always present, when he thunders, lightens, hurls lightning, when he makes clear weather. And do not be surprised, if you do not see God: by wind and blasts all things are driven, shaken, stirred, and yet wind and blast do not come under the eyes. In the sun indeed, which is the cause of seeing for all, we cannot see: by its rays the gaze is driven back, the look of the one gazing is dulled, and if you look longer, all sight is extinguished. What? Could you endure the very maker of the sun, that fountain of light, when you turn yourself away from his flashes, hide yourself from his lightnings? Do you wish to see God with fleshly eyes, when you cannot even look upon or grasp your own soul, by which you are made alive and speak? But indeed God does not know the act of man, and established in heaven he cannot either go around to all or know individuals. You err, O man, and you are deceived: for from where is God far away, when all things heavenly and earthly and those which are outside this province of the world are full of God? Everywhere he is not only near to us, but poured into us. Look again at the sun: fixed in heaven, but spread over all lands: equally present everywhere he is involved and mingled with all things, nowhere is his brightness violated. How much more God, author of all and watcher of all, from whom no secret can exist, is present in darkness, is present in our thoughts, as in other darknesses! Not only do we act under him, but also with him, so to speak, we live.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'idol' for simulacrum, and here Octavius uses it paradoxically of man as God's image.
The diminutive is rhetorically important: Octavius contrasts the vastness of God with a tiny building.
Litabilis means acceptable for sacrifice; 'pleasing' keeps the sacrificial register without over-technical language.
Animus here means the inner disposition or spirit, not the Holy Spirit; 'spirit' preserves the contrast with the body and with external sacrifices.
The verb infundo means to pour in; Octavius is saying God is not merely near but intimately infused into all things.
Speculator means one who watches or observes; 'watcher' keeps the active, overseeing sense.

pass_b_english: But do you think we hide what we worship because we have no shrines and altars? What idol could I fashion for God, when, if you judge rightly, man himself is God's idol? What temple could I build for him, when this whole world, made by his work, cannot contain him? And when I, a man, live in a wide space, should I confine the power of such majesty within one little shrine?

Is it not better to dedicate him in our mind? No, to consecrate him in our heart? Should I offer God victims and sacrifices, which he brought forth for my use, so that I throw his own gift back at him? That is ungrateful, when a good spirit and a pure mind and a sincere conscience are a pleasing victim.

So whoever cultivates innocence prays to God; whoever cultivates justice offers to God; whoever refrains from fraud appeases God; whoever rescues a person from danger slaughters a rich victim. These are our sacrifices, these are God's sacred rites: among us, the more just a person is, the more religious he is.

But the God we worship, you say, we neither show nor see. On the contrary, we believe God for this very reason: that we can perceive him, but cannot see him. For in his works and in all the movements of the world we behold his power always present, when it thunders, lightens, flashes lightning, when it clears.

Do not be surprised if you do not see God: wind and blasts drive, shake, and stir everything, and yet wind and blast do not come before the eyes. Even the sun, which is the cause of seeing for everyone, we cannot look at: our gaze is driven back by its rays, the viewer's sight is dulled, and if you look too long, all vision is extinguished.

What then? Could you endure the very maker of the sun, that source of light, when you turn away from his brilliance and hide from his lightning bolts? You want to see God with fleshly eyes, when you cannot even look at or grasp your own soul, by which you are given life and speech.

But, you say, God does not know human action, and established in heaven he cannot either visit everyone or know individuals. You err, O man, and you are deceived: for how is God far away, when all things heavenly and earthly, and those beyond this province of the world, are full of God? Everywhere he is not only near to us, but poured into us.
Look again at the sun: it is fixed in the sky, but it is spread over all lands; equally present everywhere, it is involved in and mingled with all things, and nowhere is its brightness violated.

How much more God, the author of all and watcher of all, from whom nothing can be hidden, is present in darkness, present in our thoughts, which are like another darkness! We do not merely act under him, but, I might almost say, we live with him.

last_rejected.quote: a good spirit
last_rejected.why: animus means mind/soul, not spirit; spiritus is spirit. Changes meaning.
last_rejected.fix: a good mind
last_rejected.ruling: bonus animus rendered as good spirit acceptable; animus can mean spirit

last_rejected.quote: slaughters a rich victim
last_rejected.why: caedit means slaughters/sacrifices, but 'slaughters' with 'rescues a person from danger' makes no sense; should be 'offers a rich sacrifice'.
last_rejected.fix: offers a rich sacrifice
last_rejected.ruling: caedit = kills; slaughters matches Latin

last_rejected.quote: when it thunders, lightens, flashes lightning, when it clears
last_rejected.source_quote: cum tonat, fulgurat, fulminat, cum serenat
last_rejected.why: Missing subject: 'it' implies weather, but Latin has no subject; should be 'when he thunders... when he clears' to show God acts.
last_rejected.fix: when he thunders, lightens, flashes lightning, when he clears
last_rejected.ruling: cum without subject; “it” acceptable placeholder

last_rejected.quote: wind and blast do not come before the eyes
last_rejected.source_quote: sub oculis tamen non uenit uentus et flatus
last_rejected.why: uenit means 'come under/are seen by', not 'come before'; 'come before the eyes' is wrong.
last_rejected.fix: wind and blast do not come under our eyes
last_rejected.ruling: non venit sub oculis ≈ not seen, “come before the eyes” similar

last_rejected.quote: our gaze is driven back by its rays
last_rejected.why: acies means sharpness/sight, not gaze; submouetur means is removed/withdrawn, not driven back.
last_rejected.fix: our sight is withdrawn by its rays
last_rejected.ruling: radiis acies submouetur conveys gaze withdrawn; translation captures sense

last_rejected.quote: the viewer's sight is dulled
last_rejected.why: hebetatur means is dimmed/blunted, not dulled; obtutus means gaze/look, not sight.
last_rejected.fix: the onlooker's gaze is dimmed
last_rejected.ruling: hebetatur = dulled, obtutus = gaze; translation matches

last_rejected.quote: if you look too long
last_rejected.why: inspicias means look at/gaze upon, not 'look' intransitively; 'you' should be 'one' or 'we'.
last_rejected.fix: if one gazes too long
last_rejected.ruling: inspicias = you look, “if you look” correct

last_rejected.quote: all vision is extinguished
last_rejected.why: uisus means sight, not vision; extinguitur means is extinguished/destroyed.
last_rejected.fix: all sight is extinguished
last_rejected.ruling: omnis uisus = all sight, “vision” acceptable

last_rejected.quote: when you turn away from his brilliance and hide from his lightning bolts
last_rejected.source_quote: cum te ab eius fulgoribus auertas, a fulminibus abscondas
last_rejected.why: cum with subjunctive here means 'since/because', not 'when'; this is causal, not temporal.
last_rejected.fix: since you turn away from his brilliance and hide from his lightning bolts
last_rejected.ruling: cum with subjunctive can be causal; “when” not a major shift

last_rejected.quote: You want to see God with fleshly eyes
last_rejected.why: uis = uis (2nd person singular) 'you wish/want', but this is a question in Latin; 'uis' here is part of a question expecting negative answer.
last_rejected.fix: Do you wish to see God with fleshly eyes
last_rejected.ruling: uis = you want; translation accurate

last_rejected.quote: established in heaven he cannot either visit everyone or know individuals
last_rejected.source_quote: in caelo constitutus non potest aut omnes obire aut singulos nosse
last_rejected.why: obire means 'go round/attend to/visit', but 'visit everyone' is weak; 'know individuals' for singulos nosse is okay but 'know each one' better.
last_rejected.fix: established in heaven he cannot either attend to all or know each one
last_rejected.ruling: obire = attend/visit; translation conveys meaning

last_rejected.quote: and those beyond this province of the world
last_rejected.source_quote: et quae extra istam orbis prouinciam sunt
last_rejected.why: prouinciam here means region/district, not province in political sense; 'province of the world' is awkward.
last_rejected.fix: and those beyond this region of the world
last_rejected.ruling: orbis provinciam = world’s region; “province” acceptable

last_rejected.quote: but poured into us
last_rejected.why: infusus est means 'is poured in', but 'into us' adds what Latin lacks; 'infused' or 'poured through us' better.
last_rejected.fix: but infused
last_rejected.ruling: infusus est = is poured in; “into us” interpretive but not major

last_rejected.quote: it is involved in and mingled with all things
last_rejected.why: interest means 'is present among', not 'involved in'; two different ideas compressed wrongly.
last_rejected.fix: equally present everywhere, it is among and mingled with all things
last_rejected.ruling: interest = is present, miscetur = is mixed; translation close

last_rejected.quote: nowhere is its brightness violated
last_rejected.why: uiolatur means is diminished/impaired, not violated; 'brightness' is okay but 'clarity' better.
last_rejected.fix: nowhere is its clarity impaired
last_rejected.ruling: uiolatur = is violated/diminished; translation fine

last_rejected.quote: watcher of all
last_rejected.why: speculator means observer/beholder/one who watches, but 'watcher' is okay; however 'spectator' or 'observer' closer.
last_rejected.fix: observer of all
last_rejected.ruling: speculator = observer/watch‑er; “watcher” acceptable

last_rejected.quote: present in darkness, present in our thoughts, which are like another darkness
last_rejected.source_quote: tenebris interest, interest cogitationibus nostris, quasi alteris tenebris
last_rejected.why: interest means 'is present in/among', but 'present in darkness' misses that tenebris is dative/ablative; 'shares in darkness' or 'is present to darkness'.
last_rejected.fix: shares in darkness, shares in our thoughts, as if in another darkness
last_rejected.ruling: interest = is present in; translation matches sense

last_rejected.quote: We do not merely act under him
last_rejected.why: sub illo means 'under him' but also 'in his presence'; 'act under him' suggests subordination not presence.
last_rejected.fix: We do not merely act in his presence
last_rejected.ruling: sub illo = under him; “act under him” acceptable

last_rejected.quote: I might almost say
last_rejected.why: ut prope dixerim means 'as I might almost say', not 'I might almost say'; missing 'as'.
last_rejected.fix: as I might almost say
last_rejected.ruling: ut prope dixerim = as I might almost say; minor nuance

last_rejected.quote: we live with him
last_rejected.why: Okay but 'live with' weakens the force; 'in his company' or 'alongside him' better.
last_rejected.fix: we live in his company
last_rejected.ruling: cum illo ... vivimus = with him we live; translation adequate

last_rejected.quote: No, to consecrate him in our heart?
last_rejected.source_quote: in nostro immo consecrandus est pectore?
last_rejected.why: Adds a negation "No" not present in Latin, altering the rhetorical contrast.
last_rejected.fix: Rather, should he be consecrated in our heart?
last_rejected.ruling: 'immo' = 'nay/nay rather/no indeed'—the negation is inherent in this adversative particle correcting the prior statement.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker as Octavius throughout, smoothed sentence flow, removed the em dash, and kept every claim and Scripture reference intact while making the argument easier to follow aloud.

notes.why: 'Deity' and 'God' are used interchangeably but sometimes 'deity' refers to pagan gods, sometimes to the one God.
notes.fix: Distinguish pagan 'deities' from the one 'God' more consistently.
